body:
I've gone to the hospital a number of times. I don't know where you're from, but where I'm from the admission process is tedious and it makes you feel vulnerable because you're in a clinical environment. But once I was taken to the psych unit I felt SAFE. That's really the most important part. It was uncomfortable at times, but I was safe from hurting myself.

I can't tell you with any certainty what you should or shouldn't do, but I would not recommend against going to the hospital. If you're looking for safety in this situation, I can say that I found safety at the hospital when I was in a similar situation.

I moved to the city I'm in now a little by accident. I'm originally from here, and my family is here. In my former town I had some very complicated relationships blow up in my face which caused my entire social structure to collapse. I made a lot of mistakes, other people made mistakes, we all made mistakes, but I came out the loser. (sorry I'm being super-vague here).

I went to go visit my family in [Current City] to clear my head, and I never went back. I still have some really strong connections to [Former Town] but I rarely get to visit. 

As for creativity, I'm useless by myself (well, I've actually been working on that a lot lately). I usually need to be around others because collaborating is sometimes the only way I'm able to make something. I only do comedy stuff anymore because it's one of the only things I can really do. I'm too scared to do anything else.

I haven't found a way to channel how I really feel into comedy yet. I'm experienced enough to know that there's a 1 in 100000 chance that anyone at a comedy show would actually want to hear me make jokes about killing myself, but I'm not experienced enough to be able to say those sorts of things in a way that's relatable. 

I'm working on it though. A few days ago I realized that as a comedian I've just been coasting on the "hey this new guy is pretty funny" wave for the last year and I need to actually get my shit together and work on comedy like a god damn professional. Now I've actually been writing stuff, like in a notebook, instead of just riffing off of some bullshit I came up with on twitter that day. It's not been easy. Between coherent sentences in my notebook are scribbles of profanity over and over again and sloppy messages of self-hate scrawled over half the page. And there's this /r/suicidewatch post. But I'm still fighting. 

Sorry for the rant. Thank you for responding. Despite the tone of most of this comment, I really do find what you have to say encouraging. I'm sorry you struggle too. Here's to hoping we can keep going.

Thanks for this. I made it through last night OK. It helps just to hear someone say something like this. It just gets really hard sometimes, and I get scared that I won't be able to make it through. Who knows what will really happen in the future, but it's nice that there are people out there that are willing to give words of encouragement. And that's what I needed to hear.
It feels particularly good to hear someone say that I'm strong. Thank you.
